device.name: LeIsaac SO101 PickOrange Direct (Isaac Lab simulation)

facts.text: LeIsaac registers LeIsaac-SO101-PickOrange-Direct-v0 with entry point leisaac.tasks.pick_orange.direct.pick_orange_env:PickOrangeEnv and config PickOrangeEnvCfg
PickOrangeEnv is a concrete direct task: it adds six subtask observations and implements _check_success with mdp.task_done
The single-arm direct task declares action_space = 6
IsaacLab converts an integer space specification to Box(low=-inf, high=inf, shape=(spec,))
The single-arm joint order is shoulder_pan, shoulder_lift, elbow_flex, wrist_flex, wrist_roll, gripper
Each action is multiplied by the configured action_scale and written as the robot joint position target
The direct task sets action_scale = 1.0
The base observation_space dictionary declares joint_pos (6), actions (6) and joint_pos_target (6)
The front and wrist cameras are 640 x 480 RGB cameras
The policy observation group carries joint_pos, joint_vel, joint_pos_rel, joint_vel_rel, actions, ee_frame_state, joint_pos_target and the RGB camera images
PickOrangeEnv adds the six subtask_terms observations for picking and placing each orange
The direct env reward is 0.0
The episode times out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1 unless never_time_out is set
The direct task sets decimation = 1 and episode_length_s = 25.0
The default simulation timestep is 1/60 s
max_episode_length is ceil(episode_length_s / (sim.dt * decimation))
never_time_out, manual_terminate, auto_terminate and return_success_status default to False
The task succeeds only when every orange is within x/y (-0.10, 0.10) and height (-0.07, 0.07) of the plate, and the arm is at its rest pose
The reset signature is reset(seed=None, options=None)
step takes a torch tensor, moves it to self.device and returns obs_buf, reward_buf, reset_terminated, reset_time_outs and extras
step resets terminated or timed-out environments before collecting the returned observations
SO101Leader constructs a FeetechMotorsBus with port=self.port and calls connect in its constructor
The pinned IsaacLab submodule states SPDX-License-Identifier BSD-3-Clause
The upstream package requires Python >=3.10
The isaaclab extra pins isaaclab[isaacsim,all]==2.3.0

determinism.notes: reset(seed) selects Python's random.Random for the fake's initial joint offsets; the upstream uses the Isaac Lab torch RNG and its object/camera domain randomization, so one seed does not reproduce the upstream trajectory

gaps: analytic F0 model: the joints follow the commanded target directly; no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuators, sensors, noise or domain randomization are modelled

the fake returns 4 x 4 x 3 RGB arrays for the front and wrist cameras; the upstream cameras are 640 x 480 x 3 (source/leisaac/leisaac/tasks/template/single_arm_env_cfg.py:50-83) and no rendering is modelled
the fake uses one environment and Python's random.Random; the upstream is vectorized with a leading num_envs dimension and uses the Isaac Lab torch RNG

the fake never reports task success: terminated stays False; upstream terminates when all three oranges are in the plate ranges and the arm is at rest (source/leisaac/leisaac/tasks/pick_orange/mdp/terminations.py:47-56), which needs contacts the fake does not model

the upstream observation_space is the cfg-derived dict (joint_pos, actions, joint_pos_target and the two cameras) while _get_observations returns a 'policy' dict plus 'subtask_terms'; the fake declares the structure it actually returns
the observation is a small fixed-size stand-in: the real front and wrist image dimensions are 640 x 480 x 3, and ee_frame_state, joint velocities and the per-orange subtask flags are placeholders
no snapshot or restore: the fake exposes no get_state/set_state
the upstream environment and the sim backend were not run; this package is checked on the fake backend only

only fake is declared: the inherited generic gymnasium.make fallback is not a supported live adapter. It lacks task registration, cfg/application bootstrap and numpy-to-torch/batch adaptation (the native step calls action.to(self.device), enhance/envs/direct_rl_env.py:32-36); the upstream observation_space also differs from the observations it returns

the native constructor owns a global SimulationContext and prints to stdout (dependencies/IsaacLab/source/isaaclab/isaaclab/envs/direct_rl_env.py:100-116); close clears callbacks and that global instance (:483-503), and reset can wait for textures without a timeout (enhance/envs/direct_rl_env.py:146-148). These lifecycle requirements are absent from the fake

the fake resets the scene stand-in before returning timeout observations, as native step does (enhance/envs/direct_rl_env.py:82-107), while retaining the cached last action; its initial action buffer and reset joint jitter remain placeholders

the upstream integer action specification creates an unbounded Box; the isolated R0 fake preserves that space. fixtures/operator-limits.example.json is an optional operator envelope for the fake, not a device limit or a required deployment default
the repository also includes SO101Leader, which opens a serial motor bus from its constructor (devices/lerobot/so101_leader.py:20-51); it is never instantiated by this simulation contract

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the declared analytic fake stops advancing and keeps its state and cached targets readable; no step or world reset is accepted while latched. mhs.safety.reset releases only the latch and advances no ticks. No pause or stop of an external Isaac Sim application or serial SO101Leader is provided; the serial device is outside this package
